curve.title: Drag the pin along the curve
curve.intro: The pin is your projection. Drag it — or use the slider under the chart — and the ticked subjects' exam marks rise or fall together to land there. Move any exam slider below and the pin follows.
curve.chartLabel: Distribution of NSW HSC aggregates with a draggable projection pin
curve.liveAgg: Aggregate {agg}. Type an ATAR and press Enter — the ticked subjects adjust to reach it.
curve.goalDefault: Type an expected or target ATAR and the ticked subjects are adjusted to build that set.
curve.goalMax: {Label} set: every ticked subject is at 100% and the ATAR tops out at {atar}. Tick more subjects to reach {want}.
curve.goalMin: {Label} set: every ticked subject is at 0% and the ATAR can't go below {atar}.
curve.goalOk: {Label} set built for an ATAR of {want}: ticked subjects moved {delta} marks {each}from {from}.
curve.focusHelp: Ticked subjects all rise or fall by the same number of marks. Unticked subjects stay where they are.
curve.focusEmpty: Enter internal marks on the subjects page first.
curve.noteNoFocus: Tick at least one subject — otherwise dragging the pin has nothing to move.
curve.noteMax: Every ticked subject is at 100%. This combination tops out at an aggregate of {agg} (ATAR {atar}). Tick more subjects to go higher.
curve.noteMin: Every ticked subject is at 0%. The other marks hold the aggregate at {agg}.
curve.noteMoved: {who} moved {delta} marks {each}from where the drag started.
curve.noteIdle: Drag the pin to see how far {who} would need to move. Every other number on the page moves with it.

projection.title: HSC exam marks
projection.intro: Each slider is an HSC exam mark out of 100. The blended mark averages it with the internal mark; the scaled figure is what UAC adds to the aggregate.
projection.scenText: What-if marks are whatever the sliders show right now. Save them as your expected or target set, then load either one back at any time.
projection.noInternal: No internal mark yet — enter it on the subjects page.
projection.dropped: {n} of {units} not counted — outside the best 10
projection.bandTrack: Blended mark on the band ladder
projection.bandNext: Band {band} needs an exam mark of {exam}+
projection.bandOut: Next band out of reach this exam

compare.title: Expected vs target
compare.intro: Your two saved sets side by side. Type straight into the table to adjust either one — the pins on the curve move with it.
compare.partial: * Some subjects have no saved mark in that set, so their what-if mark is used instead.
compare.none: Nothing saved yet. Set the sliders and press “Save as expected”, or type marks into the table.

units.title: The ten units that count
units.hint: Scaled points per unit, out of 50. The best 2 units of English always count; the rest are the best 8 of what's left.
units.slots: {n} slots still empty — add more subjects.
units.slots1: 1 slot still empty — add more subjects.

split.title: Two halves of 250
split.intro: Ten counting units, 50 points each, 500 in total. Half of every unit is school assessment and half is the HSC exam — so internals can earn at most 250 raw points and the exams at most 250.
split.exam: To earn in the HSC exams
split.intFewUnits: Only {n} counting units so far — at most {cap} of the 250 is reachable.
split.intFewUnits1: Only 1 counting unit so far — at most {cap} of the 250 is reachable.
split.intFull: {pct}% of the internal half. Locked once tasks are submitted.
split.extFoot: {pct}% of the exam half at the what-if marks.
split.note: The 250 + 250 split is of raw marks. UAC scales each course before adding them up, and the scaled total sets the ATAR. The gap between the two is the cost (or gain) of scaling.

impact.title: Where marks matter most
impact.intro: 5 more exam marks in one subject, everything else held. A guide to where effort pays off, not a promise.
impact.listLabel: Subjects ranked by estimated ATAR gain
impact.empty: Enter internal marks on the subjects page to see where marks matter most.

plan.title: Plan the shortest path
plan.intro: Pick a target ATAR and the planner finds the fewest extra exam marks that reach it — one mark at a time, always to whichever ticked subject lifts your aggregate most. The pin spreads marks evenly instead; the difference is how much smarter effort can save.
plan.result: extra exam marks reach an ATAR of {atar}.
plan.zero: You're already projected at or above {atar} — no extra marks needed.
plan.unreachable: Even 100% in every ticked subject only reaches {atar}. Tick more subjects or lower the target.
plan.saving: An even spread would need {even} — this plan saves {saved}.
plan.noSaving: An even spread needs about the same here.
plan.evenUnreachable: An even spread can't reach it at all.
plan.applied: Plan applied — undo to go back
plan.assumption: Assumes every exam mark is equally easy to earn, which real exams aren't. Built on the same estimated scaling as the rest of the page.
plan.needTicked: Tick at least one subject in “Subjects the pin moves”.

breakdown.title: The full breakdown
breakdown.summary: Expected vs target side by side, the ten units that count, and how the 250 + 250 raw points split.
